blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Due to the size of Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi), heavy rains and strong winds are expected to affect several parts of Luzon on Wednesday, even though the storm is not expected to make landfall in the country, the state weather bureau said. According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), Rosal was last spotted 990 kilometers (km) east of Northern Luzon, carrying maximum sustained wind speeds of 215 km per hour (kph) and gustiness of up to 265 kph.
